sources.note: Biography: accession 1537, grand-ducal title 1569, botanical gardens Pisa 1544 and Florence 1545.

sources.title: Uffizi Galleries: History
sources.note: 1560 offices for thirteen magistracies and workshops; 1737 dynasty and family pact; public opening 1769.

sources.title: Istituto degli Innocenti: History
sources.note: Foundling hospital founded before Medici duchy; wet nurses and rural foster care; grand-ducal administration with French interruption.

sources.title: Istituto degli Innocenti: Identifying tokens
sources.note: Bulk of surviving tokens 1827 to 1921; rarer late seventeenth-century objects in baptism files; earlier descriptions in registers.

sources.title: Museo Galileo: Accademia del Cimento
sources.note: Academy 1657 to 1667 under Leopoldo and Ferdinando II; experiments and publication.

sources.title: Museo Galileo: Fifty-degree thermometers, inventory 79
sources.note: Twelve glass thermometers, Florence, mid-seventeenth century; alcohol liquid, black and white enamel divisions.

sources.title: Ferdinando I: Costituzione Livornina, manuscript LJS 379
sources.note: Primary text transcription from University of Pennsylvania Schoenberg Collection manuscript LJS 379; opening grant (first article), phrase abitare con le uostre famiglie; dated Florence 10 June 1593.

sources.title: Ministry of Culture, SIUSA: Jewish community of Livorno
sources.note: 1591/1593 privileges, worship, property, study, Hebrew printing; open quarter rather than ghetto.

sources.title: Tuscan Regional Council: Leopoldina, Article LI
sources.note: Introduction note 1 reproduces 1786 death-penalty abolition and notes partial restoration four years later.

sources.title: Florence State Archive: History of Tuscan civil registration
sources.note: French system 1808, Lorraine restoration 1814, central office 1817, marriage and birth examples, union 1860.

sources.title: Lombardia Beni Culturali: Spanish rule in Milan
sources.note: Francesco II died 1535; imperial/Spanish government; tax assessment completed 1560 and burden of privileges.

sources.title: Lombardia Beni Culturali: Austrian rule, 1700 to 1796
sources.note: 1706 transition, eighteenth-century reforms and interruptions, French suppression of interim government 19 May 1796.

sources.title: Municipality of Milan: History of the Sforza Castle
sources.note: Castle became barracks during Spanish 1535 to 1706, Austrian 1706 to 1796, French 1796 to 1814 and later Austrian rule.

sources.title: Policlinico di Milano: Foundation anniversary
sources.note: Foundation 1456; lead foundation book and symbolic vessels; 1458 papal approval and lay administration.

sources.title: University of Milan: The Ca’ Granda latrines
sources.note: Latrine corridors beside wards; rainwater channels; drainage under canal to fields; construction and funding over centuries.

sources.title: University of Milan: Visit the Ca’ Granda
sources.note: Bath courtyard built in fifteenth century; early seventeenth-century use for servants and nurses.

sources.title: Pinacoteca di Brera: History
sources.note: Academy collection founded 1776; museum formally established 1809 with works from suppressed religious houses.

sources.title: Pinacoteca di Brera: The palace
sources.note: State acquisition after Jesuit suppression 1773; teaching, botanical garden, observatory and library; public library 1786.

sources.title: Teatro alla Scala: History
sources.note: Commission after 1776 fire, Maria Theresa, Piermarini, opening 1778 with Salieri.

sources.title: Teatro alla Scala: History of the boxes project
sources.note: Ownership records 1778 to 1920, archive basis and gaps; theatre as elite social space.

sources.title: Fondazione Luigi Einaudi library: Dei delitti e delle pene, 1764
sources.note: Digitized second revised edition, 1764; exact original Italian title, published by Andrea Bonducci.

sources.title: Treccani: The problem of capital punishment
sources.note: Scholarly discussion of Beccaria’s 1764 anonymous Livorno publication and penal reform.

sources.title: Lombardia Beni Culturali: Mantua in the eighteenth century
sources.note: Last Gonzaga departure 1707, transfer to Austrian rule 1708, subsequent administrative changes.

sources.title: Lombardia Beni Culturali: Bergamo under Venice
sources.note: Venetian institutions until March 1797, with earlier interruptions.

sources.title: UNESCO: Venetian works of defence
sources.note: Sixteenth- and seventeenth-century bastioned fortifications including Bergamo; response to gunpowder weapons.

sources.title: Lombardia Beni Culturali: Filanda Fumagalli Ottolina
sources.note: 1721 cadastral parcel 46, Giovanni Cottica, arable and vines; regional mulberry/silk cultivation; later industrial building.

sources.title: Museo del Violino: The Cremonese 1715
sources.note: Curator Fausto Cacciatori on Stradivari, court commissions and later instrument provenance.

sources.title: Archivio della Liuteria Cremonese: Cremonese violin
sources.note: 1715 Cremona; exact Latin label transcription; body 35.7 cm and provenance.

sources.title: Lombardia Beni Culturali: Museo del Violino
sources.note: Workshop moulds, templates and tools; G form associated with Cremonese 1715.

sources.title: Biblioteca Teresiana: Mantua’s first public library
sources.note: Public opening 30 March 1780; institution’s historical teaching account.

sources.title: Firenze University Press: Mantua’s scientific theatre
sources.note: Academic study of Bibiena theatre and 1767 contract; scientific/civic meetings and selected performances, exclusions.

sources.title: Warburg Institute: L’arte di ben cucinare
sources.note: Catalogued facsimile of Bartolomeo Stefani’s Mantua 1662 cookbook, including banquet material.

sources.title: Museo Galileo: The electric battery
sources.note: Volta, 1800; alternating zinc/copper and wet cardboard disks; continuous current by chemical action.

sources.title: Lombardia Beni Culturali: Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia legislation
sources.note: Imperial patent 7 April 1815 creates kingdom from Austrian Italian territories.

sources.title: Vatican Labour Office: Historical territorial state
sources.note: Historical account distinguishes territorial Papal State, ending 1870, from Holy See and later Vatican City.

sources.title: Vatican Museums: Coronation of Charlemagne
sources.note: Christmas 800 event; Renaissance painting uses Leo X and Francis I portraits, referring to later politics.

sources.title: Roma Capitale: Basilica of Santa Prassede
sources.note: Ninth-century rebuilding under Paschal I, reused granite columns, mosaics and San Zeno chapel for mother Theodora.

sources.title: Ministry of Culture: San Zeno mosaics
sources.note: Mosaic dating 817 to 824 from inscription and Liber Pontificalis; papal portraits include nineteenth-century restoration.

sources.title: Vatican Apostolic Library: History
sources.note: Sixtus IV’s bull 15 June 1475, appointment of Platina and financial arrangements.

sources.title: Vatican Apostolic Library: Italian historical account
sources.note: Reading regulations and external loans; surviving registers 1475 to 1547, Vat. lat. 3964 and 3966.

sources.title: Vatican Museums: Sixtus IV appoints Platina
sources.note: Melozzo fresco from original library; identifiable papal nephews and inscription praising patron.

sources.title: Santo Spirito in Sassia: Foundling wheel
sources.note: Institutional site: wheel probably present in fifteenth century, bell, nuns and wet nurses; older children accepted through door.

sources.title: Roma Capitale: Fountain of Moses
sources.note: 1585 to 1589 works, reuse of aqueduct, hill supply; exact 1587 secondary Latin inscription and criticism of statue.

sources.title: Jewish Community of Rome: History
sources.note: 1555 Paul IV bull, forced residence, property sale, yellow mark and work restrictions; community museum account.

sources.title: Jewish Museum of Rome: Historical account
sources.note: Italian capture and annexation of Rome 1870 ended territorial papal government.

sources.title: Holy See: Lateran Treaty, 11 February 1929
sources.note: Primary treaty distinguishes settlement after Rome’s annexation from creation of Vatican City.

sources.title: Ministry of Culture, Antenati: Spanish Viceroyalty of Naples
sources.note: Spanish phase 1503 to 1707; Pacichelli’s 1703 description of twelve provinces.

sources.title: Royal Palace of Naples: Service charter
sources.note: Palace begun in 1600 for Spanish viceroys, Domenico Fontana.

sources.title: Royal Palace of Naples: Ceramics of the viceroys
sources.note: Well excavation 1999 to 2000, around 5,000 objects and ceramic fragments; water/rubbish interpretation, Italian and Spanish wares, late-sixteenth-century Ming bowl.

sources.title: Banco di Napoli Historical Archive: Monte della Pietà
sources.note: Foundation 1539 for interest-free pawn loans, deposits and royal recognition as bank 1584.

sources.title: Banco di Napoli Historical Archive: Life of the banks
sources.note: Text retrieved in full search index: precious-object loans averaged 6%; Pietà accepted linen/wool/silk; interest-free loans capped.

sources.title: Banco di Napoli Historical Archive: History of the banks
sources.note: 1587 Annunziata bank supported orphanage/hospital/girls’ school; 1589 Santa Maria del Popolo bank connected to Incurabili hospital.

sources.title: Conservatorio San Pietro a Majella: History
sources.note: Early conservatories cared for poor and abandoned children; sixteenth-century religious music and seventeenth-century professional expansion.

sources.title: Municipality of Naples Historical Archive: Water tribunal
sources.note: Finding aid: Carmignano aqueduct expenses 1629, water concessions 1633 to 1778, earlier tribunal minutes.

sources.title: Treccani, Dizionario Biografico: Giambattista Basile
sources.note: Scholarly biography: posthumous publication of Neapolitan Lo cunto de li cunti 1634 to 1636, literary tales and interludes.

sources.title: Benedetto Croce edition: Basile bibliography, page LXXXVI
sources.note: 1891 scholarly edition facsimile transcribes original 1634 title page Lo Cunto de li Cunti; sample uses that attested historical title.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Shared narrative follows Medici duchy/grand duchy and Lorraine successors. Coverage 1530 to 1650 and 1650 to 1878 is retained, not asserted as state dates. Inspected source geometry has far-northern Florence extent requiring future geometry correction; this text does not certify borders.

Shared changing-government narrative; source geometry and index are separate phases. Milan 1650/1700 includes a far-southern extent inconsistent with the core duchy. Do not infer continuous Austrian rule to 1800 from the polygon.

Early and later territorial papal segments share one narrative with ninth-century material. Coverage 800 to 900 and 1100 to 1878 leaves gaps and crosses actual 1870 ending; Napoleon-era interruptions also absent from source intervals.
